briefs.task:
Plan the rest of Thrum's road to delivering the engine, as a project-level plan that brings water and clouds into it.

Purpose. The owner wants work lined up continuously toward the V1 exit in docs/BUILD-PLAN.md, so builders always have a next milestone, and wants water and clouds finished and consolidated. Today only PLATFORM-RUNTIME-MAC M2 and APPLE-TILE (G3t) are planned and open; everything after them is unplanned.

Water and clouds are built in the Broadsides repository at /Users/ryannel/Workspace/Broadsides, not here. Water is on branch codex/water-rust-system, with notes/water/DESIGN.md, DESIGN-PLAN.md and HANDOFF.md. Three spikes on 10 November left results on branches claude/fable-hull-release, claude/fable-near-waterline and claude/fable-foam (notes/water/FABLE-*.md on each). Two cloud paths, a baked library and a procedural one, were built by separate Codex agents in Broadsides; find their branches and notes there. docs/design/decisions/SEA-AND-CLOUD-PORT.md governs bringing them into Thrum: it says Thrum wasn't ready on 6 November and that the owner schedules porting. The owner has now asked for both to be finished and consolidated. Decide, with reasons, what finished means for each, whether that finishing happens in Broadsides first or as Thrum modules, and where in the build order the port's readiness conditions are met.

Done means: the project plan (module map, build order, contracts and a brief per module) covers the remaining work to the V1 exit plus water and clouds; each module that can start next has its design, plan and done-when file, so a builder can start it; and the build plan's active section points to it. List anything that needs an owner decision, such as port timing or spending, in your result rather than deciding it.

Boundaries. Don't change the definitions of PLATFORM-RUNTIME-MAC M2 or APPLE-TILE, because builders are on them. Read Broadsides but don't change it.
Revise CREATOR's design and plan as docs/evidence/CREATOR/design-review.md asks

CREATOR M3 has failed review four times, three of them on the same finding: M3.1's fresh-reader proof can't be done by the milestone's reviewer, because the review skill and project settings load engineering guidance before any item is read (docs/evidence/CREATOR/M3-review.md and its history). A lead-commissioned fresh agent (Claude Opus 5.5, permitted documents only, ordered read log) did run the exercise from a clean checkout and succeeded; its record is committed under docs/evidence/CREATOR/, but reviewers treat it as historical evidence because the plan's assumption says the reviewer runs the proof. No product defect has been found. Re-plan M3.1 so its proof is reachable: for example, an independent fresh agent commissioned by the lead, never the builder, with a read log and captures the reviewer judges from the record, or another arrangement you find better. Also look at M3.4: the fourth reviewer couldn't drive the native panel because Computer Use can't target the unbundled starter executable or see its panel window; decide whether the item, the starter's packaging or the evidence route should change. Keep the items' meaning; record the change and the reason.

The hourly workspace-tests check on main (`./dev check-all`, with a 10 s per-test limit and one rerun alone) keeps failing on timeouts. Merges are refused while main fails, so every builder stalls. Most of the failures are CPU tests that sit just under the limit even on a quiet machine. In a passing run at 747909d1c, 42 tests took over 6 s. 19 of them are in thrum-river-model::it, at 9.3 to 9.9 s, and thrum-river-model also times out most often when the Mac is busy. The other slow tests are in v1-game, water-scene, thrum-render, thrum-water, thrum-water-model, thrum-sea, thrum-network, thrum-core and thrum-clouds. The full list, with seconds, is below.

Plan the fix in the module that owns each test's code, as an item on its current milestone or as its next milestone, whichever lets it land soonest. The owner's standing rule is the fastest suite possible: small worlds and CPU-first tests, with soaks and long runs in the long-tests tier on main (`./dev long-tests`), not in the per-merge or workspace runs. Each slow test should either check the same behaviour on a smaller case so it runs well under the limit (a target of 2 s on a quiet machine is my assumption, and the owner can overturn it), or move to the long-tests tier with the reason recorded. thrum-river-model comes first.

Done: each owning module's plan and done-when file carry the item, `./dev check-docs` passes, and the files are left for the plan command to commit.
